question: What part of the NRCB2 transport test is established practice, and what part is a project-specific validation combination?
establishedMethods: NIRCam detector footprints and physical detector gaps are documented by STScI.
DOLPHOT uses WCS alignment and publishes matched-star, residual, PSF-star, central-adjustment, aperture-star, and warning diagnostics.
Artificial-star tests are an established way to measure completeness and photometric bias in crowded fields.
Independent parsing, preregistration, holdouts, and conditional-risk reporting are established validation practices in their respective fields.
rc71Combination: RC71 transfers one frozen, outcome-blind detector-tile qualification contract from NRCB1 to NRCB2, preserves every raw diagnostic receipt, classifies support-outside warnings separately from support-inside failures, and requires an independent standard-library parser before allowing the next detector. This is a project-specific combination of established components, not a claimed new theorem or new photometry algorithm.
noveltyBoundary: No claim of methodological novelty is made without a broader literature search and expert review. The contribution of this cycle is a falsifiable cross-detector transport receipt and a sharper failure boundary.
validityConditions: The parameter file and DOLPHOT binary hashes equal the preregistered values.
Only photsec differs among detector baselines.
Expected image membership is fixed from WCS before the photometric outcome is read.
Every expected NRCB2 exposure passes the published quality diagnostics.
Every warning line is typed and independently reproduced.
breakConditions: Any parameter is changed after reading NRCB2 results.
A WCS-supported image fails alignment, PSF, or aperture qualification.
An unsupported image produces a positive alignment solution inconsistent with the frozen partition.
Node and Python disagree on a diagnostic row, warning type, receipt hash, or gate decision.
